research_question: How much of the exact-cosine versus Q.ANT periodic-response error is explained by bfloat16 quantization alone, and how much remains after a bfloat16 exact-cosine control?
observations: Exp013 found monotonic frequency-dependent mismatch: mean absolute error rose from 0.002459 at k=1 to 0.015967 at k=8.
Exp013 also found a strongly structured phase-bin error profile.
Exp013 intentionally combined bfloat16 conversion with calc_kan_layer_fprop, so it cannot yet isolate quantization from the toolkit periodic approximation.
hypothesis: bfloat16 quantization explains only part of the Exp013 discrepancy; after comparing Q.ANT output against an exact-cosine control computed from the same bfloat16-quantized inputs and parameters, a structured residual error will remain and increase with frequency.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if the Q.ANT-versus-bfloat16-control residual is small relative to the original exact-float-versus-Q.ANT error across all pre-registered frequencies, or if its frequency dependence largely disappears.

comparisons: float32 exact cosine vs exact cosine after bfloat16 quantization
exact cosine after bfloat16 quantization vs Q.ANT

limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Synthetic scalar sweep does not reproduce learned activation distributions.
The bfloat16 control approximates the numerical conversion path and does not claim to reproduce physical hardware effects.
